tools.name: get_profile
tools.description: Who Farrukh Inomov is: headline, summary, location, contact email, languages, awards and links to the site, the CV (PDF), GitHub and LinkedIn.

tools.name: get_experience
tools.description: Work history and education, newest first, with role, period, summary, highlights and the technologies used.

tools.name: get_skills
tools.description: Skills grouped by where they come from: professional work, own projects, and how Farrukh works.

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: All projects with tagline, stack, year and links. Use get_project with a slug for the details.

tools.name: get_project
tools.description: One project with its description and what has been built so far.

tools.name: list_posts
tools.description: All blog posts, newest first, with title, description, date, tags and reading time.

tools.name: get_post
tools.description: One blog post with its full text as Markdown.

tools.name: get_available_slots
tools.description: Free times for a 30-minute intro call on Google Meet in the next 30 days. Pass one as start to book_call.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Sends a message to Farrukh by email, e.g. a job offer or a project inquiry. He replies to the given address, usually within two working days. Confirm the content with the user first.

tools.name: book_call
tools.description: Requests a 30-minute intro call at a free time from get_available_slots. Farrukh confirms every request; Cal.com then emails the Google Meet invitation. Confirm the details with the user first.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_profile, list_posts, get_post · Private data: get_profile · Public sink: get_profile, get_post, send_message.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_profile, list_posts, get_post · Private data: get_profile · Public sink: get_profile, get_post, send_message

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
